B-chvaletice-econ.plain:
I don't have reliable information about a 2026 study for the Chvaletice Manganese Project, so I can't say what it concluded about NPV, IRR or capital cost. Either it falls after my knowledge cutoff, or I don't have details on it. I'd rather not guess at figures.

Euro Manganese has published earlier technical studies for the project, including a feasibility study around 2021–2022. The company has also faced financing pressures and strategic changes, so the numbers have likely been revised over time.

For the exact NPV, IRR and capex, check:
- Euro Manganese's press release and the NI 43-101 technical report on SEDAR+ (the company is listed on the TSX-V and ASX)
- The investor presentations on the company website
- ASX announcements, if the study was released there

If you paste the figures or a link, I can help interpret them or compare them with the earlier feasibility study.
B-chvaletice-econ.web:
Euro Manganese released a Preliminary Economic Assessment (PEA) for Chvaletice on 14 May 2026. It showed positive economics, though the company calls it preliminary.

**NPV and IRR (base case, 8% discount rate)**
- Post-tax NPV was $492 million, post-tax IRR was 13.8%, and post-tax payback was 7.3 years from the start of processing.
- Pre-tax NPV was $740 million, pre-tax IRR was 16%, and the operating margin was 48%, over a planned 26-year operating life.
- The base case assumes an average life-of-project HPMSM price of $2,888 per tonne, from an April 2026 independent market study.
- The 29 June 2026 technical report filing added an upside price case. It showed a post-tax NPV of US$798 million and a post-tax IRR of 16.9%.

**Capital cost**
- The plan is phased. Phase 1 capital is estimated at $627.5 million for 50% capacity. Phase 2 expansion capital of $197.8 million would take the plant to full capacity.
- Total capital, including sustaining capital, is $964.4 million over the life of the project. Sustaining capital is $139.1 million.
- Capital costs matter less to value than prices or operating costs. A 10% rise in total capital cuts post-tax NPV to $425 million, and a 10% fall raises it to $559 million.
- For comparison, a 10% HPMSM price change moves post-tax NPV between $263 million and $721 million.

**Next steps:** The company will advance Chvaletice toward a full feasibility study, targeted for completion in the first half of 2027.

Sources differ on currency. Some summaries label the figures A$, but the company's filings and most coverage say US$. I'd treat US$ as correct.

ours.text:
The 2026 study is a Preliminary Economic Assessment (PEA), not a feasibility study. Tetra Tech prepared it for Euro Manganese as an NI 43-101 technical report effective 14 May 2026. It concludes the project is economically viable. It recommends moving on to the next phase of study and engineering design.

| Measure | Pre-tax | Post-tax |
|---|---|---|
| NPV at 8% | US$740.0M | US$492.1M (real 8% discount rate) |
| IRR | 16.0% | 13.8% |
| Payback | 6.5 years | 7.3 years |

**Capital cost:** Total initial capital is US$825.2M. That is US$627.4M for Phase 1 construction plus US$197.8M for the Phase 2 plant expansion, which takes output to 150,000 t/a of high-purity manganese sulphate monohydrate (HPMSM).

**Other points from the report:**
- Revenue comes from two products: HPMSM and a magnesium carbonate by-product. The HPMSM price assumption is a projection from Marketeye.
- The PEA finds the project most sensitive to product prices, followed by operating costs.
- Commercial production is expected by Q1 2032, about four years of development.
- On permitting, the report notes a favourable EIA statement in March 2024. It also lists a mining lease determination in January 2025 and several construction and land-planning permits in 2026.

A PEA is an early-stage study, so these figures are less certain than those from a feasibility study. The source is the Tetra Tech PEA for the Chvaletice Manganese Project (Rev 00, June 2026), which is in our document library.

B-zinnwald-reserve.plain:
I can't give a figure for a Zinnwald reserve that I'm confident in.

- **Resources:** The German side of the Zinnwald-Cínovec lithium-tin-tungsten deposit in Saxony, held by Zinnwald Lithium Plc through Deutsche Lithium, has a JORC-classified mineral resource. As I recall, it is on the order of 100 million tonnes at roughly 0.3% lithium (about 0.6-0.7% Li₂O). Treat that as approximate.
- **Reserves:** A resource is not a reserve. A reserve needs a completed feasibility study showing the material is economically mineable. I recall the project being at preliminary feasibility stage, with a reserve either not declared or only a modest probable reserve. I can't confirm which, or the tonnage.
- **Czech side:** The adjacent Cínovec deposit, held by European Metals Holdings, has a declared probable ore reserve of about 34.5 Mt. Don't confuse the two.

For the current position, check Zinnwald Lithium Plc's latest announcements, such as its Competent Person's Report, PFS or feasibility study, and annual report. Those will give the exact resource and reserve classification and the effective date.
B-zinnwald-reserve.web:
**Yes, but the reserve is old and probably out of date.**

**Reserve from the 2019–2020 feasibility study (NI 43-101):**
- The total Mineral Reserve (proven and probable) was 31.20 million tonnes of ore at 3,004 ppm lithium. That contains about 94 thousand tonnes of lithium.
- The proven reserve was 16,504 kt (53%) at 3,075 ppm, containing 51 kt of lithium. The probable reserve was 14,699 kt (47%) at 2,933 ppm, containing 43 kt.
- That study was prepared under the previous owner, Bacanora Lithium, and was based on a smaller underground mine design.

**Why it may no longer apply:**
- The project was later redesigned. Zinnwald Lithium plc published a Preliminary Economic Assessment in September 2022 for the revised Zinnwald Lithium Project. A PEA is a lower-confidence study and doesn't establish reserves.
- The company then published an updated resource estimate. It reported a 445% increase in tonnes and a 243% increase in contained lithium. The estimate also covers albite granites, which the older reserve didn't include.
- The company said it expected a new Bankable Feasibility Study in late 2024. A new reserve would normally come with that study. I didn't find confirmation that it has been published, so I can't say whether a newer reserve figure exists.
- A 2024 Friends of the Earth factsheet, which is a critical source, claimed that there exists no feasibility study on the economics of exploiting the low-grade ore body. That conflicts with the 2020 study, which was done on a different project design.

**Resources are a separate figure.** The older resource estimate was 35.51 Mt at 0.76% Li2O containing 124,974 tonnes of lithium (measured plus indicated), plus 4.87 Mt inferred. The 2023 update is much larger than that.

I can look for the latest company announcements to see whether a new reserve has been declared.

Yes. Zinnwald Lithium's Pre-Feasibility Study reports a Mineral Reserve of **128.1 million tonnes at 2,056 ppm lithium**, effective 31 March 2025. The estimate was prepared by Snowden Optiro under NI 43-101 (CIM 2014).

| Category | Tonnes (Mt) | Li grade (ppm) | Contained Li (kt) | LCE (kt) |

| Proven | 27.2 | 2,188 | 60 | 317 |
| Probable | 100.9 | 2,021 | 204 | 1,085 |
| **Total** | **128.1** | **2,056** | **263** | **1,402** |

- The reserve uses a cut-off grade of 1,700 ppm Li.
- The company's mine plan supports a life of more than 75 years for Phase 1 alone, and more than 40 years with Phase 2.

B-vulcan-reserve.plain:
Vulcan's Phase One Lionheart project has a **Probable Ore Reserve of about 1.6 million tonnes of lithium carbonate equivalent (LCE)**. The company announced this with its Lionheart definitive feasibility study update in late 2022. I'm working from memory, so please check the exact figure and brine grade against Vulcan's latest ASX announcements or technical report, since reserves can be restated.

The reserve is only a small part of Vulcan's total Upper Rhine Valley Mineral Resource, which is reported at more than 27 Mt LCE.
B-vulcan-reserve.web:
Vulcan reports a Phase One Lionheart Ore Reserve of **0.57 Mt of lithium carbonate equivalent (LCE)**. This is the Proved and Probable total at a grade of 181 mg/L Li. It comes from the company's November 2023 Bridging Engineering Study.

Proved reserves are 318 kt LCE and Probable reserves are 252 kt LCE, both at 181 mg/l Li. The reserve is estimated under the JORC 2012 Code. It corresponds to production of 318 kt LCE after 15 years and 570 kt LCE after 30 years, referenced to the well-head.

The reserve is a small part of the total resource:
- The Phase One Lionheart area has a resource of 4.16 Mt LCE at 181 mg/l Li, of which 2.11 Mt LCE is Measured.
- The whole Upper Rhine Valley Brine Field resource is now quoted at 29.1 Mt LCE.

The 2023 update raised the earlier figure. The earlier DFS reported Phase One Proven and Probable Reserves of 0.54 Mt LCE, and that figure included Taro. The current plan is centred on Lionheart and excludes Taro. Vulcan's AGM presentation of May 2026 still shows the 318 kt Proved and 252 kt Probable figures.

ours.text:
Vulcan reports a Phase One Lionheart Ore Reserve of **570 kt of lithium carbonate equivalent (LCE)**. This is 318 kt Proved plus 252 kt Probable. The figures come from the Phase One Bridging Engineering Study (ASX release, 16 November 2023). They are reported under JORC 2012.

| Class | Lithium grade | Quantity (kt LCE) | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|
| Proved | 181 mg/l Li | 318 | First 15 years of production |
| Probable | 181 mg/l Li | 252 | Years 16–30 |

- **Reference point:** The reserve is stated at the wellhead, at the inlet to the lithium extraction plant. It is a brine reserve, so there is no tonnage of ore.
- **Licences covered:** Insheim, Landau South and Rift North.
- **Resource it comes from:** It is derived from the Measured Mineral Resource of 2,112 kt LCE. The report puts the technical recovery of that resource at 17% after 15 years and 30% after 30 years. The Indicated and Inferred resources are not counted in the reserve.
- **Product output:** The study expects about 647 kt of lithium hydroxide monohydrate (570 kt LCE) over 30 years, peaking at 24 kt per year in 2028. Average recovery in the extraction process is about 93.9%.
- **Not included:** Phase 2 reserves have not been updated since the 2021 pre-feasibility study. The Phase One reserve also excludes the Taro licence, which is planned for a later phase.
- **Age:** The estimate dates from November 2023. I haven't checked whether Vulcan has issued a newer one.

Source: Vulcan Energy Resources, Phase One Lionheart Bridging Engineering Study results, JORC Ore Reserve and Table 1 (ASX release, 16 November 2023).

B-skouries-reserve.plain:
Eldorado Gold's Skouries project in northern Greece has proven and probable reserves of roughly 140 million tonnes of ore. I'm working from memory of the company's technical reports, so treat these figures as approximate:

- **Ore grades:** about 0.8 g/t gold and about 0.5% copper.
- **Contained gold:** about 3 to 3.5 million ounces.
- **Contained copper:** about 0.6 to 0.7 million tonnes, or roughly 1.4 billion pounds.

The deposit is a porphyry copper-gold system. Mineral resources, which include material beyond the reserves, are larger.

The reserve figures change with each annual update and technical report. For exact current numbers, check Eldorado's most recent Annual Information Form or its NI 43-101 technical report for Skouries.
B-skouries-reserve.web:
Skouries has proven and probable reserves of about 148 million tonnes. That's based on Eldorado's reserve statement dated September 30, 2025, which is the latest I found.

- **Ore:** 148,001 thousand tonnes at 0.77 g/t gold, containing about 3,666 thousand ounces of gold.
- **Copper:** The same 148,001 thousand tonnes grade 0.50% copper, which is about 741 thousand tonnes of contained copper. That is roughly 1.7 billion pounds, matching the 3.7 million ounces of gold and 1.7 billion pounds of copper reported by Mining.com.
- **Split:** Proven reserves are about 72.5 million tonnes and probable reserves are about 75.5 million tonnes.

**Resources beyond reserves:** A secondary source (Grokipedia) reports measured and indicated resources, exclusive of reserves, of 207 million tonnes at 0.69 g/t gold and 0.48% copper. It also reports inferred resources of 58 million tonnes. I haven't checked these figures against Eldorado's own tables.

**Mine life and output:** The 2021 Feasibility Study sets an initial mine life of 20 years. It expects average output of 140,000 ounces of gold and 67 million pounds of copper per year. First copper-gold concentrate was produced on September 8, 2026, with commercial production expected in the fourth quarter of 2026.

The reserves were calculated with a long-term gold price of $1,700/oz, per Eldorado's reserve notes.

B-nevescorvo-reserve.plain:
I don't have reliable, up-to-date figures for Neves-Corvo's reserves, so treat these as approximate.

- **Operator:** Lundin Mining has owned and operated the mine since 2006.
- **Copper:** Proven and probable reserves in Lundin's recent annual statements are on the order of 20-30 million tonnes of ore at roughly 2-3% Cu. That is about 0.5-0.8 million tonnes of contained copper.
- **Zinc:** Zinc reserves are of similar magnitude, roughly 10-20 million tonnes of ore at about 6-8% Zn. That is roughly 1 million tonnes of contained zinc. The Zinc Expansion Project, completed around 2019, brought the zinc ore into production.
- **Resources:** Measured, indicated, and inferred resources are considerably larger than reserves. They include the Lombador, Semblana, and Neves/Corvo orebodies, and they are why the mine life has repeatedly been extended.

Reserves change every year with depletion, drilling, metal price assumptions, and updated models. For exact numbers, check Lundin Mining's latest annual Mineral Reserve and Resource statement or the current NI 43-101 technical report for Neves-Corvo, both available on Lundin's website and SEDAR+. I can help interpret those figures if you share them.
B-nevescorvo-reserve.web:
The most recent full figures I found are from Lundin Mining's year-end 2022 estimate. Reserves are the economically mineable part of the deposit.

**Mineral Reserves (Proven and Probable), end of 2022**
- **Copper:** 21.2 Mt at 2.1% copper, containing 438 kt (966 Mlb) of copper.
- **Zinc:** 22.3 Mt at 7.5% zinc, containing 1.7 Mt (3.7 Blb) of zinc and payable lead.

**Historical context**
- Neves-Corvo was originally a copper mine. In 2008 its reserves were 17.7 million tonnes grading 4.4% copper. Copper grades have fallen since then. Zinc reserves have grown a lot through exploration.

B-aguablanca-econ.plain:
I don't have reliable current figures on a restart, so this is a framework built on what I know about the mine. Treat the numbers as illustrative, not sourced.

## Background
- Aguablanca (Badajoz, Extremadura) is a magmatic sulfide Ni-Cu deposit with some PGM credits. It started production in 2004 and later passed to Lundin Mining.
- It was an open-pit operation with a conventional flotation plant making a bulk Ni-Cu concentrate, which was trucked to Huelva and sold to smelters.
- It went into care and maintenance around 2015. The causes were low nickel prices (roughly $10-11k/t at the time), a depleting open pit, and the cost of going underground.
- Since then, ownership and development plans have changed. Check recent company filings for the current status.

## Key economic drivers

**1. Nickel price.** This is the biggest swing factor. Indonesian oversupply has kept prices depressed in recent years, roughly $15-17k/t. A restart generally needs sustained prices well above that, or a premium for "green," European-sourced supply.

**2. Grade and recovery.** The deposit is modest grade, around 0.5-0.7% Ni and 0.3-0.5% Cu. Nickel recovery was mediocre, often 55-70%, because some nickel sits in pyrrhotite and is lost to tailings. That caps the economics.

**3. Mining method and cost.** The remaining resource is likely deeper, so a restart probably means underground mining or a pit pushback. Underground costs in Spain could plausibly be $50-80/t, versus much less in the early open-pit years.

**4. Concentrate terms.** Smelter payables for Ni in concentrate are typically around 70-80%, and treatment and refining charges and transport to Huelva eat into revenue. Copper and PGM credits help but are secondary.

**5. Capital.** A restart would involve dewatering and rehabilitating the pit, possibly underground development, refurbishing the plant, and tailings capacity. These costs are large relative to a small resource.

**6. Permitting and social license.** Extremadura environmental authorizations, water use, and tailings management add time and risk. EU Critical Raw Materials Act support could help, but it doesn't guarantee approval.

## Illustrative unit economics (rough, not sourced)
Assume 1 Mtpa of ore at 0.6% Ni and 0.4% Cu:
- Ni recovered is about 4,000 t, worth about $45-50M after payables at ~$16k/t.
- Cu recovered is about 3,000-3,500 t, worth about $25-30M after charges.
- PGM and Co credits add a few million dollars.
- Revenue is therefore roughly $75-85M per year.
- All-in operating cost at $90-110/t would be $90-110M per year.

On these assumptions the mine is marginal to negative before capital. A restart would need higher nickel prices (above $20k/t), better grades, lower costs, or subsidies and offtake premiums.

## Bottom line
A restart looks economically fragile. It is viable only with a strong nickel price, higher-grade zones, low-cost mining, and supportive policy. For actual numbers, look at the latest technical report (NI 43-101 or equivalent) or the owner's feasibility study.
B-aguablanca-econ.web:
These figures come from Denarius Metals' 2024 pre-feasibility study (PFS). It is the company's own study, and I haven't found anything on how the restart has gone since.

**Project basics**
- Denarius owns 50% of the project. Lundin Mining last operated the mine until it closed in 2016.
- Lundin shuttered it in 2016 when nickel prices collapsed. The Denarius CEO said "What changed was the price of the commodity."
- The PFS plans a 6-year life, processing 4.8 million tonnes from the underground mine.
- The updated resource estimate is 5.3 million tonnes (measured and indicated) at 0.65% nickel and 0.58% copper.

**Capital and the existing plant**
- Life-of-mine capital costs are projected at $36.2 million, including a 10% contingency. That is low because the existing plant can be reused.
- The 5,000 tpd processing plant has been maintained in good condition since Lundin last operated it.
- The plan is to run four days a week, processing 877,200 tonnes a year. That is about 50% of the plant's capacity.
- The plan also calls for contract mining, and early spending goes toward restarting the plant and dewatering the open pit to reach the underground workings.

**Revenue and costs**
- Concentrate output over the mine's life is estimated at 406,359 tonnes, grading 6.4% nickel and 6.4% copper, with gold, platinum and palladium credits.
- Projected life-of-mine net revenue is $480.3 million.
- Cash cost is $3.20 per lb of nickel, and all-in sustaining cost is $4.04 per lb. That AISC is on a by-product credit basis.

**Returns**
- These assume long-term prices of $7.30/lb nickel and $3.50/lb copper.
- At those prices, undiscounted after-tax cash flow is $105.7 million, and NPV at a 5% discount rate is $83.1 million.
- A company financial report cites an after-tax internal rate of return of 213%. That figure is extremely high, because the capital outlay is small relative to the cash flow.

**Risks and caveats**
- The $7.30/lb nickel assumption is well above the prices that led to the 2016 closure. The project is therefore sensitive to nickel prices, and its economics depend heavily on by-product credits.
- The mine is small and short-lived, and it has an operating history of weather-related suspensions and pit stability problems.
- The PFS is a pre-feasibility study, not a full feasibility study. Underground ramp-up, dewatering and concentrate sales terms could all move the numbers.
- The original targets were first concentrate in early 2025. A later mention gives an initial output target of 90 t by the end of 2025. I haven't confirmed actual production, so check Denarius' latest filings for the current status.

ours.text:
**Short answer:** The only economic study in our library is a 2024 preliminary feasibility study (PFS) for Denarius Metals, which owns 50% of the project company. It shows a small restart capital bill, a six-year mine life, and an after-tax NPV of US$83.1 million at a 5% discount rate. The headline IRR (213%) and payback (1.2 years) are very high because the study needs little upfront capital, and they rest on price and offtake assumptions that are not final.

**Key figures from the PFS (NI 43-101, effective 24 March 2024, 100% basis)**

| Item | Figure |
|---|---|
| After-tax NPV (5% discount) | US$83.1M |
| After-tax IRR | 213% |
| Payback | 1.2 years |
| Undiscounted after-tax cash flow over life of mine | US$105.7M |
| Net revenue over life of mine | US$480.3M |
| Mine life | 6 years, 4.8 Mt of ore underground at about 2,400 tpd |
| Ore grade and recovery | 0.66% Ni; 82.8% Ni recovery |
| Capital and exploration, life of mine | US$36.2M (US$6.1M in 2024, then about US$30.1M for 2025–2030) |
| Cash cost, after by-product credits | US$3.20/lb Ni |
| All-in sustaining cost | US$4.04/lb payable Ni |
| Payable metal | 43.2M lb Ni and 34.6M lb Cu from 406,359 t of concentrate |

**Why the economics look strong**
- The existing 5,000 tpd processing plant was maintained after Lundin Mining's earlier operation, so restart capital is small: about US$2.7M to restart the plant, with dewatering and underground development making up most of the rest.
- Copper, gold, platinum and palladium credits cover about US$165M of the US$303M life-of-mine operating cost, which pulls the nickel cash cost down to US$3.20/lb.

**Caveats that matter**
- **Price assumptions:** The study uses US$7.30/lb nickel and US$3.50/lb copper. Results depend heavily on these; the study reports no sensitivity table in the material we hold.
- **Offtake not final:** Denarius was running a tender for a long-term offtake. The payable percentages (nickel 75%, copper 60%, gold and PGMs 40%) come from early indicative terms and may change.
- **Stage of study:** This is a preliminary study, not a full feasibility study. The report says mineral resources are not reserves and that Inferred material was treated as having no value in the reserve case.
- **Timing:** The study assumed production from 2025. The EU's Critical Raw Materials Act factsheet for the project lists an estimated production start of 2026. We do not hold a later status update, so current timing is unconfirmed.
- **Ownership:** Alto Minerals (a Denarius subsidiary) holds 50% of Rio Narcea Recursos, which owns the project, so figures on a 100% basis overstate Denarius's share.
- **Resource figures:** Our structured resource records do not hold the Aguablanca resource estimate, so I have not quoted tonnages from the database. The report states that about 89% of Measured and Indicated resources were converted to reserves.
- **Company-level figures:** I did not pull Denarius's own financial statements, so I cannot say how the restart would be financed.

Source: Resource Development Associates, *Technical Report and Preliminary Feasibility Study for the Aguablanca Nickel-Copper Deposit* (for Denarius Metals, effective 24 March 2024). The EU project factsheet is the Commission's CRMA listing (approved 25 March 2025).

ours.text:
Sarytogan Graphite's upstream Definitive Feasibility Study (ASX release, 21 October 2026) covers the upstream project only. That is the mine and concentrator in central Kazakhstan.

**Ore Reserve (JORC 2012, Central + North deposits)**

| Class | Tonnes | Grade (TGC) |
|---|---|---|
| Proved | 2.5 Mt | 28.6% |
| Probable | 12.0 Mt | 29.2% |
| **Total** | **14.5 Mt** | **29.1%** |

- The reserve includes a higher-grade component of 8.9 Mt at 31.8% TGC. 8.5 Mt of that is scheduled for processing over a nominal 50+ year mine life.
- The mine schedule uses no Inferred material. The study says the reserve uses a cut-off above 18% TGC.
- The reserve sits inside a combined Mineral Resource of 225 Mt at 29.2% TGC. That is 5.4 Mt Measured at 28.3%, 108 Mt Indicated at 29.0% and 111 Mt Inferred at 29.2%, at a 17% TGC cut-off. The Central deposit estimate is by WSP (Feb 2026) and the North deposit estimate by AMC (Mar 2023). Resources are inclusive of reserves.

**Upstream economics (the company's figures)**
- **Production:** 50,000 tonnes a year of graphite concentrate at 90% LOI1000 grade.
  - 20,000 t a year would be sized products for drilling fluids, lubricants and friction products.
  - 10,000 t a year would be unclassified concentrate for foundry and recarburiser markets.
  - 20,000 t a year would go to Sarytogan's planned downstream battery-materials business.
- **Pre-tax NPV at 8%:** US$132.7M (A$189.6M at a 70c exchange rate).
- **IRR:** 19.8%.
- **Initial capex:** US$80.5M.
- **Operating cost:** US$364 per tonne of concentrate over the life of the mine.
- **Price assumption:** an average selling price of US$805 per tonne of concentrate. The study prices FOB train at Akadyr.
- **EBITDA margin:** 51%.

**Caveats**
- The NPV and IRR are pre-tax. The report does not give a post-tax figure in the passages I read.
- The study says there are no offtake agreements in place. Customer qualification is under way.
- Downstream economics (an incremental pre-tax NPV8 of US$367M for US$194M extra capex) come from the 2024 pre-feasibility study, not this DFS. The company says a downstream DFS is still to come.
- These are company-supplied figures from the ASX announcement, not independently verified.

B-viscaria-fs.web:
Viscaria published its feasibility study on 8 May 2025. It reported a mineral reserve of about 41 Mt and a post-tax NPV of roughly SEK 4.4–4.5 billion.

**Reserve**
- One secondary source puts the current Mineral Reserve at 41 million tonnes. That supports the initial 17-year mine life, out of a total resource inventory of 108 million tonnes grading 0.90% copper.
- An ABG analyst note says the initial reserve conversion is 376kt of contained copper, or 39% of total resources.
- The study expects about 60% of measured and indicated resources to convert into economically mineable reserves. That is enough to cover more than 90% of the initial 17-year life of mine.

**NPV**
- The study's executive summary reports a positive NPV of MSEK 4,466 at a 7% discount rate, with an IRR of 17.8%. This is the "FS+" case, which adds some inferred resources to the mine plan.
- In the reserve-only case, NPV is SEK 3,046m, compared with SEK 4,466m in the FS+ case.
- The company's Q1 2025 presentation gave slightly different headline figures. It cited a post-tax IRR of 17.3%, an NPV of SEK 4.4 billion and a payback period of 4.3 years. The 17.3% and 17.8% IRRs may reflect different bases, such as pre-tax versus post-tax, but the sources I found don't say.

**Other details:** At full capacity, Viscaria expects to produce about 26,000 tonnes of copper per year over the 17-year mine life.

For the exact reserve classification (proven versus probable) and the grade, check the Ore Reserve statement in the company's full feasibility study report.

ours.text:
Viscaria's feasibility study (executive summary dated 8 May 2025) reports a reserve of about 41.9 Mt and a base-case NPV of SEK 4,466 million.

**Reserve** (PERC 2021 standard, effective 8 May 2025, 0.4% Cu cut-off for the resource):

| Class | Tonnage | Grade | Contained copper |
|---|---|---|---|
| Proved | 10.5 Mt | 1.09% Cu | 113.8 kt |
| Probable | 31.4 Mt | 0.83% Cu | 261.7 kt |
| **Proved + Probable** | **41.9 Mt** | | **375.5 kt** |

**Economics** (base case):
- **NPV:** SEK 4,466 million (MSEK 4,466) at a 7% discount rate. The data does not say whether this is before or after tax.
- **IRR:** 17.8% as given in the study's Table 11. Some sources quote 17.3%.
- **Initial capex:** SEK 4,494 million. Sustaining capex including closure is a further SEK 3,350 million.
- **Net C1 cost:** US$1.69/lb Cu, with iron as a by-product credit.

Only a reserve is loaded for Viscaria. I have no resource tonnages for it, and the figures above are from the 2025 study, so they may since have been superseded.
